[spoiler=Wellassona in a tense atmosphere as General elections approach] 
[i]Wellassonan National News - Новеллсти Нациоьнлыы Веласоньый. Sunday, 16 July, 2028[/i]

In 13 days, Wellassonans will head to the polls in what is set out to be the closest election since the transition to democracy in 1996. The election, which is taking place during a time of insecurity and uncertainty, will almost certainly decide the future of the nation.

The tensions coming up to the elections are already palpable; just over a month ago, a brawl occurred in the Diet, in which several dozen Diet members were arrested and expelled from their duties. in particular, the Left-wing Socialists and the Far-right Reform the State parties have been at each other's throats since the incident, throwing insults and accusations at each other.

In the wake of the brawl, both parties have been desperately struggling to appeal to voters. For the Socialists, the young, charismatic Kaldangan Kemurtevič has risen to the top of the party. Well known for his often unorthodox approach to politics, he has quickly gained a strong following, especially among young voters, urban voters, and Muslims, which are 3 of the most important demographic voter groups going into this election. 

However, his main opponent is not from the far-right, but instead from the Libertarians. Ipatiy Sergeev, the Leader of the Opposition and leader of the Toward the Future party, is Kemurtevič's main opponent. While  nowhere near as charismatic or young (he's 64), that might not end up mattering. Due to current PM Danil Sokolova's highly unpopular economic policies, Sergeev's own liberal economic agenda has garnered the approval of many. 

Tertiary in terms of challengers for the spot of the PM, is the choice of the Far-Right, Valya Kulikov. Her rhetoric has led her to amass a wave of followers. Running on a staunch anti-immigration platform, she has promised to end all immigration (and emigration) from Muslim-majority countries. While she states that the purpose of such restrictions is to keep Wellassona safe from criminals and terrorists, she has been panned by opponents for being Islamophobic and for attempting to undermine Wellassona's friendships with Muslim Nations.

While there are many other parties that are running for the spot as Prime Minister, none are considered to have a chance at being victorious in the election.

As election day nears, Wellassonans hold their breaths for what is set up to be the most significant election in their nation's history. After the General Election on 29th July, the PM will be chosen by the winning party by late August, and will take office and form a government by 5 October
